subject: Residency & air-gap discovery — post-call synthesis
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Priya Shah <priya.shah@novarumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Sep 2027 11:09:00 -0700
Subject: Residency & air-gap discovery — post-call synthesis

Hi Priya — thanks again for the 45-minute call this morning. Quick recap below so we’re aligned and to capture the ask for our infra/eng review.

High-level goals you shared
- Keep all PHI + model inferencing within Novarum-owned VPCs or on-prem clusters in AWS us-east-1 for the initial rollout.
- Support an air-gapped/limited-egress option for the pilot clinic environment (no outbound internet except approved endpoints).
- Maintain strict data residency and encryption-at-rest + in-transit; customer-controlled KMS/HSM is preferred.

Primary pain points / constraints
- Existing procurement and security require SOC2 artifacts and an architecture diagram showing control-plane access boundaries.
- Network team: strict egress firewall rules, only allow connections to a whitelist of Redwood endpoints over TLS on specific ports.
- Cache/infra requirement: low-latency inference near their EMR cluster; they want <150ms median token latency for 512-token sequences.

What Redwood can already do (summary)
- Private/VPC deployment with customer-managed peering and optional on-prem package.
- Support for customer-managed KMS; control-plane can be routed through an isolated control channel per agreement.
- Built-in fallback to smaller local quantized model when full model cannot be reached — useful for the air-gap use-case.

Immediate next steps (owner and ETA)
1) Mateo: capture Novarum network map and allowed egress list (they offered to send) — received by today, 9 Sep.
2) Marissa (security lead): produce SOC2 extract and short artifact set (<= 2 pages) for initial review — by 12 Sep.
3) Lauren (solutions eng): run preliminary latency feasibility with a synthetic 512-token profile in us-east-1; share expected SLOs and recommended instance types — by 15 Sep.
4) Priya/Amit: confirm procurement timeline and if they require a vendor security questionnaire (SSQ) or a one-off PO — reply in-thread.

Attachments referenced: please attach your network map (can be a simple diagram). I've attached our standard SOC2 extract and a short one-pager on deployment options for quick reference.

(Attachment: SOC2-summary-2026.pdf)
(Attachment: deployment-options-onepager.pdf)

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it and I’ll adjust. Proposing a 30-minute follow-up next week after your network/ procurement inputs — drop times that work and we’ll lock it.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Executive
Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
(Attachment: novarum-network-guidance-template.pdf)

From: Dr. Priya Shah <priya.shah@novarumhealth.com>

Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@novarumhealth.com>, procurement@novarumhealth.com
Date: Thu, 8 Sep 2027 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & air-gap discovery — post-call synthesis

Thanks, Mateo — that looks right and clean. A few clarifications:
- We will send the network map and the current firewall policy (export) by end of day today — attaching to this thread.
- Procurement: we typically request a vendor security questionnaire followed by a short tech eval; I’ve looped procurement and Amit (network lead).
- KMS/HSM: we prefer using our AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK; please confirm that Redwood supports using a customer CMK for encryption-at-rest for private deployments.

One more ask: we run periodic scans and need an explicit list of IP ranges and FQDNs you require outbound (for whitelist). Can you provide that as part of the SOC2 extract?

Thanks,
Priya
Dr. Priya Shah
VP Clinical Informatics
Novarum Health
(Attachment: novarum-network-map-v1.pdf)
